newsitem.title: USA: Consumer spending, incomes up strongly in August.
newsitem.headline: Consumer spending, incomes up strongly in August.

text.p: Consumers spent briskly in August, especially on costly durable goods like new cars, and personal incomes posted a solid gain, the Commerce Department said Monday.

Spending jumped 0.6 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $5.17 trillion after a 0.2 percent rise in July. Income from wages, salaries and all other sources also increased 0.6 percent to a rate of $6.5 trillion following a 0.1 percent July rise.
The report showed steady gains in consumer incomes, as expected, because the government previously reported that the average wrokweek was longer and hourly earnings were up in August.
Monthly incomes have been growing for more than a year. Department officials said the last time there was a decrease in incomes was in May 1995, when they fell 0.1 percent.
During August, the amount of money put into savings eased slightly to 5.2 cents out of each dollar earned from 5.3 cents in July.

The Commerce Department said private wages and salaries increased by $27.3 billion in August after declining $8.6 billion in July. Payrolls were higher in commodity-producing industries, manufacturing, distribution and service industries.

Gains in personal income, which includes wages and salaries as well as income from sources such as dividends, interest and businesses, are essential for funding consumer purchases that fuel two-thirds of national economic activity.
Consumer spending rose in five of the six months through August, with the only decline coming in June when it fell 0.5 percent.
Spending on durable goods, which includes cars, surged 3.1 percent in August to an annual rate of $644 billion in August from $624.9 billion in July.
But spending on nondurable products was flat at $1.54 trillion while spending for services rose 0.3 percent in August to $2.99 trillion.
An earlier report from the Commerce Department had shown relatively weak business at retail stores in August, with sales up only 0.2 percent afbter a slight 0.1 percent in July.
But August automobile units sales were strong.
Payrolls of manufacturing companies rose to an annual rate of $683.1 billion in August from $675.8 billion in July.
